index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure presents a two-part diagram: an upper section illustrating the YOLOv8-Pose model architecture for object pose estimation, and a lower section depicting a semi-automatic dataset generation and training pipeline. 

In the upper part, the global layout flows left to right. An 'Image Input' is shown as a grayscale image of a surgical tool, feeding into a 'Backbone' module represented by a stack of four decreasing rectangular blocks, colored light blue. This backbone extracts features and passes them to the 'Object Detection Head', also light blue, which consists of three parallel stacks of rectangular blocks. Outputs from these stacks are combined and fed into the 'Pose Estimation' module, depicted as a single white block within a purple rectangle. The final output is labeled 'Object Pose Output', showing the same surgical tool image with a bounding box and four blue keypoints indicating estimated pose. Arrows indicate forward propagation from input through backbone, detection head, and pose estimation to output.

The lower part shows a circular training pipeline with six rectangular modules connected by arrows. Starting from 'Initial Data' (light gray), the flow proceeds to 'Generate Object and Marker Masks' (light blue), then to 'Extend ST-Pose Dataset' (light blue), followed by 'Marker De-Dependence Data Augmentation' (light blue). From there, it goes to 'Train YOLOv8-Pose' (light blue), then to 'Online Inference and Data Sampling' (light blue), and finally to 'Manual Label Refinement' (light blue), which loops back to 'Generate Object and Marker Masks'. All modules in the pipeline are rounded rectangles with black borders and dark blue text. The arrows indicate the sequential steps in the iterative training process, emphasizing data refinement and augmentation to improve model robustness without relying on markers. The caption explains that the dataset uses masks generated by a modified Cutie method, and data augmentation involves substituting backgrounds and markers with different textures to achieve marker independence.
